PR surface: Source +55, Tests +210, Docs +5. Total +270 across 12 files.

target.title: Fix realtime voice-call barge-in cancellation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Realtime voice calls could keep playing assistant audio after the caller began speaking. The local MuLaw detector and the realtime provider could disagree about whether a true interruption occurred, and clearing local playback did not consistently cancel the canonical Talk turn or already-buffered Twilio audio.

## Why This Change Was Made

This refactors barge-in into one provider-neutral contract instead of special-casing an OpenAI websocket event in the voice-call transport:

- Realtime providers report an accepted interruption as `onClearAudio("barge-in")`.
- OpenAI emits that signal only after its configured speech-start policy accepts server VAD; Google emits it for `serverContent.interrupted`.
- The voice-call audio sink owns the transport action: clear the Twilio pacer and cancel the canonical Talk turn once.
- Providers that do not advertise input-audio barge-in support retain local MuLaw fallback detection.
- Late local interruptions still clear Twilio's remote playback buffer after provider output has completed locally.

The OpenAI and Google realtime contracts were checked directly before choosing the boundary. No gateway protocol or catalog surface is added.

## User Impact

Callers can interrupt realtime OpenAI and Google voice output without hearing stale buffered audio continue. Provider-confirmed interruption is the source of truth when supported; other providers keep the existing local fallback. The provider SDK documents the optional capability and typed clear reason.

## Evidence

- Current head: `2535cac4fbe0d5b9221b086d4cfd8fe9df22a932`.
- Focused post-rebase regression suite: 4 files, 128 tests passed (`src/talk/session-runtime.test.ts`, voice-call realtime handler, OpenAI realtime provider, Google realtime providers).
- Fresh whole-branch autoreview: no actionable findings, confidence 0.91.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Official OpenAI Realtime and Google Live API docs/types were inspected for the provider interruption semantics.
- Contributor live proof on macOS with Twilio + OpenAI: human speech during playback produced provider-confirmed clear of 63,840 queued bytes, `output.audio.done`, and `turn.cancelled`.

```text
2026-06-05T23:20:10.793+02:00 talk event output.audio.started
2026-06-05T23:20:12.590+02:00 [voice-call] realtime local speech detected callId=[REDACTED]
2026-06-05T23:20:13.008+02:00 [voice-call] realtime outbound audio cleared by provider barge-in callId=[REDACTED] queuedBytes=63840
2026-06-05T23:20:13.008+02:00 talk event output.audio.done
2026-06-05T23:20:13.009+02:00 talk event turn.cancelled
```

The live call was captured on the contributor's earlier implementation head; the current head preserves that path while moving the invariant to the typed provider/audio-sink boundary and expanding regression coverage to OpenAI, Google, local fallback, late buffered playback, and canonical turn cancellation. A second exact-head human phone interruption was not repeated because the maintained test host has no Twilio/OpenAI voice credentials.
